title: MercadoLibre — Q2 Print Confirms Compounder Reset
summary: MELI Q2 2026 delivered 50% YoY revenue growth (fastest in 4 years) and EPS $9.19 vs $8.83 est, validating that Mercado Pago credit-loss trajectory has inflected and margin reset is behind us. Promoted from Stalking (2026-06-27) on fundamental confirmation of the promotion trigger.
catalyst: Q2 2026 print (2026-08-05): net revenue and financial income grew 50% YoY, reached $10.17B (beat $9.86B est), EPS $9.19 vs $8.83 est. Marcelo Melamud (SVP-CAO) filed follow-on Form 4 purchases post-print. Q3 print in early November is the next dated catalyst — confirms whether the credit-book normalization and unique-active-buyer acceleration extend into H2.
thesis: MELI is the dominant Latin American e-commerce + fintech platform (screener BUY-adjacent at 73). The bear case (Mercado Pago credit losses compressing margins) that drove the Q1 multiple reset has been rebutted by Q2 results — revenue re-accelerated to a 4-year high and management raised active-buyer growth guidance. Insider buying by the SVP-CAO into the print adds an inside-view signal that management sees the credit trajectory turning. This is the compounder-at-reset-valuation setup we were stalking.
counter_thesis: Stock has already run to $1,828 (mid 52-week range $1,495-$2,548) at forward P/E ~35x — not the deep-value entry the stalking envisioned. LatAm macro (Brazil rate cycle, Argentina FX) can flip revenue growth if the Real weakens or Argentina hyperinflation persists. Mercado Pago is a credit-book-driven fintech; a single quarter of credit normalization does not eliminate the tail risk from a broader LatAm recession. Multiple compression from 35x to 25x on any deceleration would offset our upside.

ticker_rationale.MELI: Only ticker in our screener with the LatAm ecom-fintech-logistics moat. Q2 EPS $9.19 (+18% YoY beat), net revenue $10.17B (+50% YoY), unique active buyers accelerating. Screener overall_score 73, Growth sleeve, forward P/E 28-35x.

trade_construction.entry_zone: MELI $1,700-$1,850 (current $1,828 — above pre-print consolidation; wait for pullback to $1,750 preferred)
trade_construction.target_12mo: MELI $2,400 (+31%) — 32x FY27E EPS ~$75 assuming 25-30% earnings growth from FY26E ~$50-55, plus modest multiple re-rating on sustained credit-book normalization
trade_construction.stop_loss: MELI $1,475 (-19%) — closes below the 52-week low $1,495 signals the Q2 print was a head-fake and credit book is re-deteriorating
trade_construction.position_size_pct: 0.5-1.0% (On Our Radar sizing given post-print chase risk)

confidence_note: Trade construction is best-available: entry has already run +9% since original stalking filing and post-Q2 chase risk mirrors the ONON blow-up pattern (Q2 beats can still drop the stock -18% if the buy-side has already positioned). Would firm up to High Conviction if: (a) Q3 confirms 30%+ revenue growth trajectory, or (b) MELI pulls back to $1,600-$1,700 zone on macro noise without a thesis break. Position size skewed low pending an accumulation window.

catalyst_calendar.event: Q3 2026 earnings — confirms credit-book normalization thesis

MELI.action: Initiate on $1,700 pullback; skip on further extension

risks: Post-print chase risk — stock has already run and Q3 beat is largely priced in at 35x forward P/E
LatAm FX volatility (Brazilian Real, Argentine Peso) — a 15% Real depreciation would erase 20% of USD revenue growth
Mercado Pago credit book — a single-quarter normalization does not eliminate tail-loss risk if LatAm consumer softens
Multiple compression from 35x to 25x would offset 25%+ of upside even if earnings deliver

invalidation.trigger: Q3 2026 net revenue growth decelerates below 30% YoY
Mercado Pago credit-loss provisions increase >20% QoQ in Q3 or Q4
MELI closes below $1,475 for 2 consecutive weeks
